clue.text: Relatively minor attack is repulsed by warship — victory at last!

parts.note: a sub (submarine) is a submersible vessel built for warfare

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the words attack is are read backwards

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of victory

explanation.surface: A naval report: an assault is beaten off by a warship, with victory finally won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is repulsed' reverses the two words before it, giving SIDIAR; a sub, short for submarine, counts as a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A subsidiary matter is secondary, of lesser importance relative to the main one.

clue.text: Father shows anger with son

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A dad loses his temper with his boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire is to father offspring, and a sire is a male parent.

clue.text: Between beginning and end of blizzard, transport's delayed

indicators.note: between says the transport word sits inside the two outer letters
the first and last letters of blizzard are taken

parts.note: to transport is to delight or elate; the 's is the link is

explanation.surface: Snowstorm chaos: trains and buses held up all day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like vehicles but is the verb meaning to enrapture, giving ELATE inside B and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Belated means coming late, after the expected time.

clue.text: In trouble, criminal leader gets arrested, judged and imprisoned

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: arrested means held, so the trouble word holds the letter

parts.note: care means worry or trouble

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of criminal

parts.note: rated means assessed or judged

explanation.surface: A court story: a crook in trouble is arrested, tried and locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In trouble' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two pieces; 'arrested' signals that the criminal's first letter is held inside the trouble word.
explanation.definitionFit: Incarcerated means confined in prison, locked up behind bars.

clue.text: Understand belonging to trade union's the very thing

parts.note: in can mean belonging to, as in 'a member in the club'
TU is the abbreviation for trade union
it means the ideal thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Getting the point that union membership is exactly what is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to know or grasp something by instinct rather than reasoning.

clue.text: Takes flight, say, after turning up in part of airport

indicators.note: in says the turned word goes inside the airport piece

parts.note: a runway is the strip at an airport for take-off and landing

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: as can mean say, introducing an example

explanation.surface: A plane takes off after appearing on the airfield strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes flight' suggests a plane taking off, but here it means flees; 'after' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs away means escapes or flees, just as takes flight does.

clue.text: Guzzler's emptied wine bottle

indicators.note: emptied means the inside of Guzzler is removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker has drained the wine bottle dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a container for the wine, but it is the definition in its British slang sense of nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, bottle means courage or nerve, the same quality as determination under pressure.

clue.text: Protest about introduction of revolutionary form of transport

parts.note: to rail is to complain or protest loudly
ca is short for circa, about

indicators.note: introduction of means the first letter of revolutionary

explanation.surface: Demonstrators object to a radical new type of vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A railcar is a self-propelled railway carriage, a means of travel.

clue.text: New pet is only a small dog

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists their new pet is just a little puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy spaniel is a miniature breed of spaniel kept as a companion.

clue.text: Giving report about company in recession moving to new premises

indicators.note: about says the report word goes around the other piece

parts.note: relating means giving an account or report

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: A firm, hit by the economic downturn, announces it is moving to cheaper offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' suggests economics, but here it just means going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Relocating means changing one's place of business or residence to somewhere new.

clue.text: Quite insignificant aspect of conflict in Yemen

indicators.note: aspect of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A commentator dismisses one facet of the war in Yemen as trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiny is very small, so minor in scale or importance.

clue.text: We would ring, announcing beautiful women below?

definitions.text: We would ring, announcing beautiful women below?

indicators.note: below says the next piece comes underneath in this down entry

parts.note: we'd is the contraction of we would
ding is the sound of a bell ringing

indicators.note: announcing means saying out loud, so the women word is heard

parts.note: belles are beautiful women

explanation.surface: Bell-ringers promise to peal out news of the brides below.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: church bells ring to announce a marriage of a lovely bride. BELLES is heard as BELLS, placed under WE'D DING.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedding bells are the church peals rung to celebrate a marriage ceremony.

clue.text: Minor trouble stirred up by Man U spectator: I'll join in

indicators.note: stirred up means agitated and mixed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the football club Manchester United
taken as written
the I of I'll, the 'll being the link

explanation.surface: A Manchester United fan promises to join in some crowd trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: MANUSPECTATOR plus I gives fourteen letters that rearrange to the answer; Man U is Manchester United, the football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a lot of fuss over something unimportant, a small trouble blown up.

clue.text: Way loyal associate keeps fighting to end of conflict?

definitions.text: Way loyal associate keeps fighting to end of conflict?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the ally word contains the next pieces

parts.note: an ally is a loyal associate
war is fighting

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of conflict

explanation.surface: Describing how a faithful partner keeps battling until the war is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: fighting on to the end describes acting resolutely.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwartly means steadfastly and loyally, as a dependable supporter acts.

clue.text: I tried desperately to be more organised

indicators.note: desperately suggests frantic effort, signalling the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits they tried hard, and frantically, to get their life in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidier means neater, in better order, the comparative of tidy.

clue.text: Chinese person's endless courage

parts.note: a man is a person

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the courage word is cut off

parts.note: daring is boldness or courage

explanation.surface: Praise for an individual from China whose bravery knows no limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese person' reads as one phrase, but only 'Chinese' defines; 'person' gives MAN and 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the main spoken language of China, so it is Chinese in the language sense.

clue.text: One initiating romance with girl at end of old-fashioned dance

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
to romance can mean to tell fanciful lies, so one who starts such tales is a fibber

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A man begins a love affair with a girl at the close of an old-time dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' means telling tall stories, so one who initiates it is a LIAR; 'old-fashioned' looks like part of the definition but only supplies D.
explanation.definitionFit: The galliard was a lively Renaissance court dance in triple time.

clue.text: Have no time, unfortunately

parts.note: to lack something is to have none of it
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A complaint from someone too busy: they simply have no time, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence, but 'unfortunately' is the definition of an old exclamation of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackaday is an archaic exclamation of sorrow, meaning alas or sadly.

clue.text: Ruddy criminal keeping lips sealed

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the criminal word goes around the lips word

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
lips are rims, as of a cup

explanation.surface: A blasted crook keeps his mouth shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' reads as a mild British swear word, but it is the definition, meaning red; 'sealed' just completes the picture of lips kept shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddy means reddish, and crimson is a deep red colour.

clue.text: Food in part of hospital always rejected

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the always word is read backwards

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Hospital meals in one department are always sent back uneaten.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a dish served at a meal, either the main course or a starter.

clue.text: He wrote a new Morse novel

indicators.note: novel means fresh or original, so these letters are given a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer produces a fresh Inspector Morse book.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome was the English author of Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome was a twentieth-century English children's author and journalist.

clue.text: Eel-like fish seen from side of boat

definitions.meaning: a long slender coastal fish, also called the butterfish
a variant spelling of gunwale, the upper edge of a boat's side

explanation.surface: An eel-shaped creature spotted from the edge of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a slim blenny-like fish and the top edge of a vessel's side.

clue.text: Play with best mate?

parts.note: a play title, by Oscar Wilde, read as a description of a perfect spouse

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a game with their closest friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play with' looks like a verb phrase about games, but it is a noun: a stage play, Wilde's comedy, featuring the ideal partner, a mate in the marriage sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde's comedy title describes a perfect husband, the best possible marriage partner.

clue.text: 007 character is seen at opening of this film

parts.note: M is James Bond's spymaster boss

indicators.note: at opening of means the first letter of this

explanation.surface: A Bond character appears in the opening scene of a spy movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but means a thin covering, as of haze on glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A mist is a thin hazy layer or film, as on a window.

clue.text: Pal, shy when drunk?

indicators.note: when drunk signals the slurred speech of a drinker, so the throw word is said thickly

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A friend who is timid until they have had a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs the final S of TOSS into SH. 'Tosh' is British slang used to address a man, like mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a man may be addressed as tosh, much like chum or mate.

clue.text: Sheltered by clergyman, little girl's given single portion of pasta

indicators.note: sheltered by means the girl's name is placed inside the clergyman word

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral
Nell is a girl's name, as in Little Nell from Dickens
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: A girl taken in by a priest is given one helping of Italian food.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannelloni are tubes of pasta, typically stuffed and baked, served as a dish.

clue.text: Gossip about north American native

indicators.note: about says the gossip word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to yak is to chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: Idle talk concerning an indigenous person from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American native' looks like the definition, but 'native' belongs with 'north' in the surface; 'American' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is informal for an American, a person from the United States.

clue.text: Youngster, when claiming unemployment benefit, gets very little money

indicators.note: claiming means taking in, so the when word holds the benefit word

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit
a cent is a coin of tiny value

explanation.surface: A young person on benefits receives hardly any money.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit; 'claiming' signals that the word for when goes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a teenager, someone between childhood and adulthood.
